items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: And so was John of course, obviously, everybody knows.

ctx.x: Yeah, look it up. It’s online. It just came out I think. It’s really interesting when he asked her about it. And you know Alice is very spiritual you know, very much into the culture. And so was John of course, obviously, everybody knows. But I think Alice had some influence on him or it was probably mutual, that the music is more than just music. In fact in my memoir, which I hope to finish up hopefully by next year. I call it “It’s More Than Only Music” you know? More than only music you know. And that music is…

any of the literary things and so we do a careful analysis of the musical history whether it be blues, whether it be folk, or gospel or church music or whatnot, we can get a good idea of what was going on in terms of civil rights, in terms of human rights and human suffering and degradation. You can hear the cries in the music. And so that’s why I really think that the Lord Almighty gave us the blues, which seems it’s not going to ever go away you know and it has many forms. I mean almost all American music forms…
